scope: Implemented borrowed font-query identities, lazy owned payload creation and in-place ASCII language normalization; no public API change.

conclusion.allocation: Deterministic reduction of transient allocation calls and requested bytes across all measured build workloads. Paint-only 64-style build: 734 -> 411 calls, 306328 -> 298637 requested bytes. Retained and peak memory unchanged.
conclusion.timing: Inconclusive. Unpinned ordinary no-language builds suggest roughly 2-5% lower median, but other groups and CPU-2-pinned results have large inconsistent changes. Unchanged builder-record controls also moved by up to 61% in pinned runs. These runs do not establish an elapsed-time speedup or a regression.
conclusion.long_tags: Rejected initial one-byte-at-a-time hash variant regressed approximately 23-26% on 1156-byte tags. Final code hashes lowercase stack-buffer blocks; unpinned final long-tag medians are lower, while noisy pinned results remain inconclusive.
conclusion.parley: No page/PNG or Parley comparison was rerun for this patch. Do not subtract these allocation or microbenchmark results from the previous page comparison.
conclusion.output: All before/after geometry, font-instance, glyph, paint and warning digests matched per workload across final timing/allocation runs.
conclusion.instructions: Callgrind confirms lower total build guest instructions in all 22 workloads (ordinary multi-size 64 styles approximately 1.3-3.2%, paint-only Latin approximately 4.6-5.4%); this is not an elapsed-time speedup. See callgrind_record for attribution and long-tag tradeoff.

changes: QueryKey borrows family and language data from retained InlineStyle values; normalized numeric attributes preserve previous identity.
Create owned normalized FontQuery only in the HashMap vacant-entry closure; duplicate query identities do not clone payloads.
Explicit Latn/Auto fields avoid allocating and discarding the default SansSerif family Vec.
FontQuery::normalized lowercases the owned language String in place; borrowed ASCII-insensitive identity hashes 64-byte stack blocks.
Tests cover float fallbacks/clamps, signed zero, ASCII and Unicode language distinctions, multi-block hashing, family ordering/kinds, synthesis and forced hash collisions.
New allocation regression test is included in the existing CI allocation-counting command.
